subject: AI & Agents
title: Few-Shot Learning: Teaching by Example
description: A fast breakdown of Few-Shot Learning: Teaching by Example for builders.

hook.text: Show an LLM three examples of the output you want, and it figures out the pattern instantly.

buildup.text: Few-shot prompting includes examples in the prompt to guide the model's behavior.

discovery.text: The model doesn't retrain — it uses the examples as in-context patterns to follow.

twist.text: The order and quality of examples matter. Bad examples can mislead the model completely.

climax.text: Zero-shot works too — just describe the task. But few-shot is usually more reliable.

punchline.text: Show, don't just tell. AI learns from examples too.

quiz.question: What is few-shot prompting?
options: Including examples in the prompt to guide the model
Training the model on a few data points
Limiting the model to short responses

details.summary: Few-shot learning provides an LLM with a few examples in the prompt to demonstrate a desired task or format. The model generalizes from these examples without any retraining, adapting its behavior on the fly.
details.whyItMatters: Few-shot learning makes LLMs instantly adaptable to new tasks without fine-tuning. It is a key technique for getting reliable, formatted outputs from general-purpose models.
takeaways: A few examples in the prompt teach the model a new task pattern
No retraining or fine-tuning is required — it works immediately
It enables rapid adaptation to custom formats and workflows

faq.question: How many examples does few-shot learning need?
faq.answer: Typically 2-5 examples suffice for simple tasks. More examples help with complex or ambiguous tasks. Zero-shot (no examples) sometimes works, but even one example often dramatically improves consistency.

faq.question: Why does few-shot learning work without training?
faq.answer: LLMs are powerful pattern matchers. Examples in the prompt create a pattern the model continues. It leverages the model's pre-trained ability to recognize and extend patterns rather than learning new weights.
